question: Can an existing real isolated profile/unit handler execute against authentic late V11 state, without a new full500 start or bypassing time/case/GO/control bindings, and reveal the missing actual heap/external/natural-GC lifetimes?

answer.summary: The real next endpoint executes one exact next DR unit, but it is inseparable from the live installed500 operation/claim/window and its original controls. No existing late-V11 component can replay a spent or expired unit legitimately. A fresh process and DB copy cannot restore the153min application-isolate/telemetry/GC history.

scope.inspection: Only actual selected entrypoint sources, their guard dependencies, existing component scope and previously saved scalar metadata. No general code search or repeated telemetry investigation.
scope.actionBoundary: No implementation, tests/imports/AST/CLI subjects, SQL/DB/native/Docker/proc/Git/model/network actions; no original payloads, old claims/adoptions, or source modifications.
scope.division: Root separately assesses resource authorization and isolated component limits. This report proves software/temporal/state constraints and does not invent a new permission gate.

entrypoints.actualBehavior: Endpoint accepts only action+operationId+commandHash. index is accepted only by export, never next. It enters storage.withSynthetik500PreparedCommand, loads the current bound packet and validates stored content/authority before productionNext.
entrypoints.oneUnitBoundary: productionNext297–311 chooses the observed journal index internally and calls executeUnits(...,[index],true). Therefore the code genuinely performs one DR unit per HTTP request.
entrypoints.whyNotAnIsolatedReplay: There is no request field for an arbitrary old index, supplied command, callback, fake journal or token. The existing source does not expose a bypass for a late replay.

entrypoints.actualBehavior: Claims an installed unclaimed real500 operation via Auth CAS, enters index0, then executes only index0 for D-R-500.
entrypoints.limitation: A new first unit is a cold-start unit of a freshly admitted500 operation. It neither selects the authentic V11 late index nor restores previous main-isolate/collector/native allocation history. Calling it on a copy of a permanently claimed operation cannot reset that claim.

entrypoints.actualBehavior: Internal implementation of full guarded DR work. It is not exported.
entrypoints.limitation: Extracting/exporting or injecting command/claim/index would be new implementation/contract and could evade the original entrypoint proof. No such extraction is proposed.

entrypoints.actualBehavior: Real domain routine exists and is exported. The admitted adapter supplies only the selected profile, finite input token, current guards beforeGenerate/beforeSave and actual cost admission.
entrypoints.limitation: Calling this exported lower layer directly is not the actual unit handler: it omits the current operation entry/claim/next selection/evidence/finalCAS orchestration unless those original guarded callbacks and state are genuinely present. Existing-result checks may also return without generation. A fabricated callback or token would not qualify an authentic current unit.
These do not execute profile DR work or reproduce its allocation history. They cannot answer the missing live-lifetime attribution question.

mandatoryGuards.guard: Actual current packet and time-limited authority
mandatoryGuards.constraints: Exact selector, actual stored row/source/certificate binding, fresh native proof, admission expiry equal plan end, real current time, embedded actual-gate+testGO hashes, and exact operation/commit/deployment/plan/package/window. Signed content certificate is at most9h and cannot extend past plan end.
mandatoryGuards.reuseFailure: A copied database or new process does not refresh certificates, deadlines or admission. Re-signing/rebinding an old operation as current is not an existing component contract.

mandatoryGuards.constraints: Journal state running, stopRequested false, exact claim+command+plan, active time window, no inFlight, index>0, exact current index, selected unit unentered, every prior unit entered with outputs and accounted attempts; J.enter permanently marks unit entered and creates Unit60 deadline.
mandatoryGuards.reuseFailure: A previously entered/unknown/stopped unit cannot be selected again merely because resources are isolated. There is no resume/reset API for that purpose.

mandatoryGuards.guard: Actual500 active runtime and current inputs
mandatoryGuards.constraints: Original test-window/storage protection, actual500active profiles/501identities, exact manifest/end time and fresh runtime observation, native source/profile equality, briefing/date binding, fresh control reads, financial/accounting checks. These repeat at original control points.
mandatoryGuards.reuseFailure: A fake runtime envelope, stripped command, subset-profile fixture or omitted native guards would change the tested path.

mandatoryGuards.constraints: Local mock calendar explicitly does not change Date/timers/accounting/authorization. Policy requires execution day equal source day; current time must remain inside the admitted exact plan. In-flight EU unit deadline remains≤60s.
mandatoryGuards.reuseFailure: The calendar helper is not a legal time-travel facility for an old plan. It cannot revive an October20 entered unit on October21.

mandatoryGuards.constraints: Original immutable evidence persistence/readback, accounted attempts, final Auth CAS/ACK and journal advance. On failure the unit is stopped/unknown and permanent claim remains; no retry/resume on an unknown write.
mandatoryGuards.reuseFailure: Deleting evidence, clearing an entered bit/inFlight/claim, or manually installing earlier journal state to make next pass would alter the authentic state rather than observe it.

retainedLateStateFacts.observed: The scalar extract binds the original terminal runtime failure and actual J.enter/HTTP timestamps. No source-based guess of exact final persisted journal fields replaces a new state proof.
retainedLateStateFacts.consequence: The authentic terminal attempt has already been entered and failed; the current once/time guards do not make it a fresh executable next unit. Whether the exact retained final journal is stopped or unknown does not rescue the expired unit.
retainedLateStateFacts.missingCheckpoint: No qualified, still-current, unentered pre-late-unit checkpoint plus original live application isolate is identified by the existing sources/metadata. A final PGDATA snapshot is not such a process checkpoint.
retainedLateStateFacts.originalProtection: No original/canonical/Bank database may be started or modified for this question. Fresh copy isolation alone does not grant dispatch or revive a consumed case.

existingComponentBoundary.covers: One fixed current27AuthRPC workload:5reads/4CAS/18controls,3rounds/6boundaries and original full6000history/ACK/CAS/restore.
existingComponentBoundary.implication: That actor is a closed Auth/server-context component, not a generic real-profile adapter; old cases/adoptions/once receipts cannot be repurposed. No parameters expose a unit handler.

whyFreshOneUnitDoesNotAnswerTheOriginalG.databaseStateVsProcessState: An authentic late DB copy can preserve stored logical content, not V8 object identities, accumulated telemetry, JIT/allocator residence, natural-GC phase, Buffer backings or the original main-isolate lifetime.
whyFreshOneUnitDoesNotAnswerTheOriginalG.currentVsOldSource: The requested unit would run current sources under a new effective budget, whereas V11 was old full code/budget and old process trajectory. Exact current identity/source/clock framing would still be required.
whyFreshOneUnitDoesNotAnswerTheOriginalG.allowedInterpretationOnly: A newly qualified genuine unentered unit in a fresh operation could answer a narrower cold-unit working-set question. It would not establish or falsify long-run retained growth and must not be reported as the authentic late V11 lifecycle.
whyFreshOneUnitDoesNotAnswerTheOriginalG.noDataLossShortcut: Dropping already-completed outputs, changing journal/plan timestamps, bypassing GO or substituting bare domain calls cannot transform that narrower result into the original question.

smallestPermissibleNextStep.actionNow: Do not start an old case, invoke productionNext/start, generate fake GO, or prepare another native actor. Record that no existing admissible isolated late handler satisfies the combined question.
smallestPermissibleNextStep.ifQuestionChanges: Root may first define, source-only, whether a cold current unit at late-sized stored state is independently valuable. That requires a NEW explicit component contract and genuine fresh once/time/control/evidence scope; it is not available from this audit and does not answer the old153min isolate-lifetime gap.
smallestPermissibleNextStep.ifOriginalQuestionRemains: The missing heap/external/natural-GC lifetimes must be observed in a genuinely authorized current fullpath process as it reaches real completed-profile boundaries. Do not infer or initiate a full500 run: resource/GO qualifications remain open and Root owns them.
smallestPermissibleNextStep.preciseDecision: NO for the requested existing isolated authentic-late-lifetime capability. YES only for the software fact that each real current next request dispatches exactly one guarded unit, contingent on its still-valid live operation; no such existing late V11 execution context is qualified here.

handoff: Final source-only read-only release. No implementation or action authorization is implied.
